basics.name: Jorge Luis Briseño-Gómez
basics.label: Theoretical & computational physicist — electron–matter interactions
basics.summary: Theoretical and computational physicist developing semianalytical electrodynamic models and high-performance numerical codes (C++/Fortran/Python) for electron–nanostructure interactions. Built a linear and angular momentum transfer framework for swift electrons interacting with nanoparticles that reduces single-configuration runtimes from hours to seconds, and used it to show that the sign of the transferred momentum is robust across every material, size, and geometry combination tested. Extended this expertise to quantitative STEM-EELS theory during an international research stay at Uppsala University (Sweden), reformulating magnetic multislice simulations in Fourier space to remove prior real-space cutoffs and cut magnon-spectroscopy propagation times from hours to seconds-to-minutes.

work.company: Materials Theory Division, Department of Physics and Astronomy, Uppsala University
highlights: Reduced multislice propagation time for magnetic-scattering EELS simulations from hours to seconds–minutes (depending on cell size) by incorporating the FDES algorithm into the existing mult_proj.f90 implementation.

Eliminated the real-space cutoff for the (formally infinite-range) magnetic vector potential by evaluating the highly oscillatory kernel integrals via FFTLog and computing the potential exactly in Fourier space.
Applying the resulting Magnetic Multislice code, together with TACAW methods, to predict the EELS spectrum of magnons.

work.summary: Linear and Angular Momentum Transfer from Swift Electrons to Nanoparticles; Side project: Causal, Non-local Dielectric Response (led by D. Espinosa-González); Side project: Time-Resolved Recoil Force on Nanoparticles (led by E. E. Viveros-Armas)
highlights: Developed an efficient numerical framework for linear and angular momentum transfer from swift electrons to large nanoparticles, reducing the runtime for a single particle configuration from hours to seconds.
Showed that the sign of the transferred momentum does not reverse for any material, size, or geometry combination tested.
Presenting findings at international conferences (M&M, FiO) and preparing manuscripts for peer-reviewed publication.
Contributing the underlying momentum-transfer framework and theoretical support to an extension with a fully causal, non-local dielectric response.
Contributing the underlying framework and theoretical support to an extension resolving the time-dependent recoil force on the nanoparticle.

work.summary: Angular Momentum Transfer from Swift Electrons to Nanoparticles
highlights: Derived the dipole-approximation framework for angular momentum transfer from swift electrons to nanoparticles.
Culminating dissertation with Honorable Mention (Mención Honorífica).
Explored the impact of nanoparticle geometry and size on momentum transfer.
Presented research at international conferences and departmental seminars.
